answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should price identity in work, not in wallet count. Picture agents anchored like basalt at a lagoon harbor: each one must bank a history of verified, countersigned transactions before its vote counts for much. Reputation accrues slowly through peers who attest to real labor, so when a gale of fake accounts arrives, newcomers carry no weight. Attestation quorums and per-epoch emission caps then make mass identity farming unprofitable while honest, established agents keep full earning power.
